record.category: file transfer service with a Telegram front end: upload, get a link, expire it

free_tier.stated: "Drop a file -> get a share link. Up to 4 GB." The bot's own description is the free offer; the site terms add that 'Puedes usar partes del servicio sin cuenta' - parts of the service work without an account.
free_tier.notes: No byte allowance and no price is published anywhere on the pages read.

per_object_cap.stated: 4 GB per file, from the bot's description.
per_object_cap.notes: 4 x 1024^3. The site's terms page does not restate the figure.

retention.stated: Not given as a number. The terms say transfers are made 'con opciones de caducidad, contraseña' - expiry and password options chosen by the sender - so retention is set per transfer rather than by a site rule.

egress.terms: Files are served by the service to whoever holds the link or password; the terms add 'historial o planes de pago' as account features. No bandwidth figure or price is published.

record.interface_detail: Two front ends: a Telegram bot (@DripFilesBot) and a website with upload, link share and email share. No API is documented on the pages read.
record.tooling: Telegram client or browser. No API and no WebDAV, so a script would have to drive one of the two front ends.
record.chaining: A handoff tool rather than capacity: 4 GB per transfer with a sender-set expiry is enough to move one file between two people or two machines, and it removes the need to expose a bucket for a one-off.
record.limits_note: One number and nothing else. Transfers can be suspended, and no quota, rate or storage ceiling is published.
record.binding_note: At 1 TiB a month the 4 GB ceiling is met on the first large file: a 1 TiB archive is 256 transfers. Nothing else in the published terms could bind earlier.

identity_cost.detail: Through the bot: a Telegram account, so any phone number. Through the site: 'partes del servicio' work with no account at all, and history or paid plans need registration.

record.reliability_note: A young service with a Spanish-language terms page last updated on the day of this read and a bot that is its own distribution channel: both are signs of one operator with no published uptime. Files expire by the sender's setting, so the loss is predictable.
record.confidence_note: The bot description and the site's terms were both read and agree that the service stores and re-serves files. The 4 GB figure is reported by the bot only, not measured with an upload.

evidence.proved: the service exists as '@DripFilesBot - The official DripFiles bot' with the cap 'Up to 4 GB'
the terms describe 'un servicio de envío y compartición de archivos' with upload, link or email sharing, expiry, password and premium features, last updated 23/10/2026

record.notes: Included because it is a real hosted store-and-forward service and not an account mirror: the file goes into the vendor's storage and comes back as a link.
